newsitem.title: USA: Coventry sees Q2 after-tax gain $6 million.
newsitem.headline: Coventry sees Q2 after-tax gain $6 million.

text.p: Coventry Corp said Wednesday it expects to record an after-tax gain of $6 million in the second quarter on the sale of its St. Louis-area medical practices to BJC Health Systems, which closed today.

The company also said that it has sold $28 million of convertible exchangeable subordinated notes and warrants to Warburg Pincus Ventures LP and Franklin Capital Associates III LP. The proceeds of the notes were used to reduce bank debt by $20 million and for general corporate purposes. An additional $14 million of notes and warrants will be sold to Warburg following regulatory approval, it said.
Coventry said its sale of the St. Louis medical offices will enable it to sign long-term global capitation agreements with major provider organizations that in turn will reduce its medical costs.
It said the $28 million capital infusion from the first phase of the Warburg transaction solidifies its financial base.
